Daily Brief

The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster dominates international headlines as the death toll surpasses 1,000 with over 4,400 people still missing, including hundreds of workers believed trapped in hydropower tunnels [BBC World, ABC Australia, Globe and Mail]. Rescue teams from Nepal, China, India, and other nations are racing against time to reach survivors, with one Australian found alive after six days [ABC Australia]. Meanwhile, Russia escalated its aerial bombardment of Ukraine overnight, killing at least 12 people in Kyiv and surrounding regions, including an Indian national, as EU defence ministers convene in Ireland to discuss bolstering Ukraine's air defences amid interceptor missile shortages [BBC Europe, Al Jazeera, RFI English, The Hindu]. In a landmark verdict, a Las Vegas jury found former gang leader Duane 'Keffe D' Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, closing one of America's most infamous cold cases after nearly 30 years [BBC World, RNZ, Globe and Mail]. Iceland narrowly rejected resuming EU membership talks in a referendum, with 52.8% voting against despite security concerns raised by the government [BBC Europe]. In other developments, the Metropolitan Museum of Art cancelled its planned 2027 Met Gala honouring designer John Galliano following outcry over his 2011 antisemitic remarks [RNZ].

Former Gang Leader Found Guilty of Orchestrating Tupac Shakur's 1996 Murder

  • Las Vegas jury convicted Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, 63, of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon after nearly three hours of deliberation
  • Davis was accused of ordering the drive-by shooting and supplying the gun used by his nephew Orlando Anderson, who died in 1998
  • Prosecution relied heavily on Davis's own media appearances and memoir, plus recorded police interviews where he admitted being in the car

Iceland Rejects Resuming EU Membership Talks in Close Referendum

  • 52.8% of voters rejected the government's proposal to restart EU accession talks, with approximately 12,600 votes separating the two sides
  • Turnout was 82.5%, the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009, with over 225,000 people casting ballots
  • Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's government had advanced the referendum citing international tensions, including Trump's threats against Greenland
  • Debate centred primarily on fishing rights rather than security concerns; Iceland froze its EU application in 2013 over fisheries disputes

  • The museum reversed its decision to make controversial designer John Galliano the subject of an exhibit linked to the 2027 Met Gala
